description: Configuration of the backend-agnostic infer operator: the backend, the model, the prompt and response mapping, the request policy, and each backend's specialized keys.
notes: The union of OllamaSpec and VllmSpec. It embeds the same InferCommonSpec they do rather than restating it, which is what lets one document serve both backends without a second copy of output_mapping and error_channel. The specialized keys are flat and inert on the backend that does not read them: keep_alive and think are ollama's, structured_output is vllm's.

description: A paragraph of a text template document: one block of markup, wrapped to the document width.
notes: Declared in jets/agentic/template rather than in pipes_model.go, which is this table's first rows for a struct outside the cpipes package; TextTemplateSpec carries it by reference so the contract reaches the notation rather than stopping at the array. Tested first, mirroring compileElement, which reads text before elements. Q-106, settled at BB.1 2026-09-11: no kind discriminator, and the two variants are ~virtual tokens telling themselves apart by shape. That needed one relaxation - check required the discriminator column to be '-' exactly when the token is '*', which conflated having variants with having a discriminating key, and Element is the first struct whose variants are all virtual. The one-row alternative was written first and the harness refused it: a minimal config synthesised from a single Element/* row carries neither text nor elements, which is a compile failure, so a contract that cannot state the rule cannot generate a valid document.

description: A group of a text template document: children emitted in array order, with a fallback for the case where none of them emitted.
notes: Declared in jets/agentic/template rather than in pipes_model.go, which is this table's first rows for a struct outside the cpipes package; TextTemplateSpec carries it by reference so the contract reaches the notation rather than stopping at the array. The recursion of the notation lives here: a group's children are elements. A document is itself a group, which is what lets the document-level empty be one concept rather than a special case.

description: Configuration of the render transformation operator: the template it applies, the column it reads and the column the rendered text lands in.
notes: It does not embed InferCommonSpec, and the overlap is deliberate rather than missed: row_key_column, on_error, max_error_count and error_channel carry the same meanings the infer operators give them, and the other five members of that struct - model, api, the two prompt fields, output_mapping - describe a request to a server this operator does not make. Embedding would put nine inapplicable keys on every render step to save four rows.

description: Shared configuration of text template documents, named and applied by the render operator.
notes: PromptTemplateSpec's shape one array over, and copied rather than paralleled: a document declared at the configuration root can be shared by several steps and pipes. The four document fields are copied from template.Spec rather than embedded, because the engine's Spec decodes strictly and admits no comment while every element of this configuration carries one; TestTextTemplateSpecCarriesTheDocument is what keeps the two in step.

description: Renders one text template per record and augments the record in place with the rendered text.
notes: The infer token's escape is unavailable to it: infer is rewritten into an ollama or vllm step before anything else sees it, so it added no dispatch site, while render is new runtime behaviour with nothing to be rewritten into. It pays the six switches of the phase plan's section 1.6 in full, and reportsRowLevelFailures and errorChannelConfig both name it, which is what a row-level operator owes.
